title: Jaeger UUID normalizer + health prober for Tempo/Jaeger bridge compatibility
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: A subset of legacy Jaeger clients emit non-standard trace IDs (mixed-endian UUIDs and legacy 128/96-bit encodings) and occasionally set timestamps that confuse Tempo's ingestion heuristics. When these spans pass through our OTLP/Jaeger bridge they either get rejected, cause downstream assortment mismatches, or trigger health alarms on Tempo backends. Goal: Add a compatibility layer in the trace ingress path that normalizes incoming trace identifiers to a consistent canonical form, and surface a lightweight health prober that continuously validates wiring between the ingress, the normalizer, and Tempo/Jaeger backends.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingress normalizer successfully rewrites legacy/non-canonical trace IDs into our canonical 128-bit trace-id format while preserving span relationships. 2) No loss of span parentage in randomized integration tests (end-to-end test harness shows 0% parent-link failures across 50k synthetic traces). 3) New health prober emits per-backend pass/fail metrics and an aggregated boolean that integrates into existing latency/error dashboards. 4) Backwards-compat behavior toggle via config flag (off by default for private deployments). 5) Performance overhead <2% p99 ingest latency on standard load profile.
implementation_notes: Plan: (1) Introduce a Normalizer stage in the ingress pipeline that inspects trace_id/span_id encodings. (2) Apply non-destructive canonicalization rules: detect endian variants, pad/truncate 96-bit IDs to canonical 128-bit by prefixing a deterministic salt, and rewrite IDs in the OTLP envelope headers. (3) Emit mapping metadata in an opt-in header for debugging only (strip in prod unless debug-mode enabled). (4) Health prober: lightweight probe that opens a short-lived write to each configured backend endpoint and verifies an ingest -> query loop (write synthetic span, poll backend index TTL) — exposes metrics: probe_success, probe_latency_ms, probe_error_reason. Trade-offs: canonicalization must avoid collisions; we prefer deterministic salt over random UUIDs to keep traces reproducible. We will add collision checks to post-deployment canary runs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer rules, fuzz tests with legacy Jaeger clients corpus, integration harness: synthetic client -> ingress -> tempo/jaeger -> query API to confirm parent-child structure. Backpressure and perf tests using 10k traces/s profile with current CI cluster. Add test that asserts metric emission for health prober and a Grafana smoke dashboard linked below.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: ID rewrite could break consumers that rely on original raw trace_id. Mitigation: opt-in mapping header + rollout gate behind config and canary routing. Risk: increased p99 due to extra processing. Mitigation: microbenchmarks, optimize hot-path in C++ normalizer module and JIT compile the common path; fallback to fast-path when input is already canonical. Risk: potential collision when padding 96->128; mitigation: use deterministic padding scheme tied to source-namespace and validate collision rate in canary.
monitoring_and_metrics: New metrics: normalizer.rewrites_total, normalizer.rewrite_errors_total, normalizer.latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, probe.success_rate, probe.latency_ms_p95. Dashboards: trace-ingest-health (new panel), probe-failures alert (SLO: probe_success_rate >= 99.5% over 5m). Add log sample rate for rewrite errors to avoid noise.
deployment_plan: Feature branch implements Normalizer and prober behind feature flag. Canary rollout: 5% of traffic to normalizer-enabled route for 48h with continuous integrity checks from integration harness. If canary stable, increase to 25% then 100% over 4 days. For Dedicated/Private customers, leave disabled unless customer requests compatibility mode.
